A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same unfolded-GNN conformal prediction work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations and experiments on SBM, School, Flight, and Trade, including accuracy, coverage, prediction-set sizes, and temporal analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments on temporal transduction, data splits, conformal scores, and GNN architectures.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure remains dilated unfolding followed by a standard GNN and conformal calibration. Explicit feature construction and validation inputs add documentation; testing additional GNNs and score functions instantiates the existing modular procedure.

E1.justification: The four dataset domains and prediction tasks remain unchanged. The new stationary SBM control extends stationary community-detection analysis already illustrated in Section 2.1. Temporal transduction and the additional School experiments vary protocols and configurations within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained block/unfolded GCN and GAT comparisons, v2 evaluates block/unfolded GraphSAGE and JKNet in Table 12. Tables 10–11 add RAPS and SAPS alongside APS, substantially broadening the evaluated architecture and conformal-score families.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds experiments training on earlier times and calibrating/testing on later times. Appendix F evaluates six School split ratios, including the original ratio; Appendix G reserves 20% of calibration data for RAPS/SAPS hyperparameter selection. The original main-experiment protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a stationary SBM control for time-conditional coverage, split sensitivity tests, and checks of dependence on conformal scores and GNN architectures. These substantially extend v1's temporal and worst-time coverage analyses, which are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 10 GNN fits with 100 calibration/test permutations for transduction, 50 semi-inductive splits, and means with standard deviations. Additional tables use the same uncertainty reporting style; no new confidence intervals, significance tests, or explicit increase in repetitions is reported.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 retain identical numbers, but Table 5 changes: semi-inductive SBM coverage for UGAT rises from 0.879 ± 0.031 to 0.907 ± 0.031, without explaining the numerical revision. Tables 6–12 add substantial results under additional controls and protocols, rather than improvements to the unchanged main benchmark scores.

T1.justification: v2 adds the formal requirement that each represented node/time adjacency column contain a nonzero entry. The coverage theorems and proof arguments remain substantively unchanged. Moving formal exchangeability definitions into Section 2 and redefining m to include the test point do not constitute new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The central claims remain valid dynamic-graph conformal prediction through unfolding and improved predictive/conformal performance. v2 emphasizes assumption-free transduction and names temporal transduction explicitly, but both the guarantee and the historical-training/current-calibration scenario already appear in v1 Section 2.

C2.justification: v2 adds a scalability limitation: unfolding prevents independently loading time points, with representative-time acceleration suggested as future work. It also revises the conditional-coverage interpretation from neither method achieving validity to UGAT often doing so. Existing drift and fully inductive limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents identity-matrix features for unattributed graphs, unlabeled global nodes, feature dimensions, and validation inputs. These clarify implementation without establishing an implementation change. The code-access location and reported CPU/training times are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting RAPS, SAPS, GraphSAGE, JKNet, and two scaling approaches, while removing the Vovk (2012) conditional-validity reference. It explicitly positions unfolding as a modular CP–GNN interface; the principal novelty comparisons with earlier graph-conformal and unfolding research remain.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, Section 2 expands the inference-regime and input explanations, and formal assumptions move from the appendix into the main text. The temporal-analysis and conditional-coverage appendices exchange order. Much of the main experimental narrative and overall section structure is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a contribution overview with representation and split diagrams plus the embedding illustration. The three main GAT temporal figures are consolidated into a six-panel Figure 3. Seven additional tables, revised captions/highlighting, and the conference layout substantially change visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 explains the representation and inference regimes more clearly and gives the modularity claim broader empirical support through sensitivity and architecture checks. These gains are tempered by unexplained numerical revisions to Table 5, validity markings below the stated 0.90 target in Tables 5–6, and severe SAPS undercoverage in Table 10 without adequate discussion. The unchanged core results remain supported, but these reporting issues limit the overall improvement.
